rationale: Both candidates independently nail the one substantive unresolved ground-truth concern (FLASHINFER_ATTN allow-listed for quant but never consumed) with precise file/line evidence and concrete fixes, and both also independently surface the same unlisted-but-valid ring-SP/SAGE-silently-dropped bug, giving strong cross-validation. Y edges ahead on precision/craft: it verifies claims with actual executed Python snippets (e.g. the AttnQuantSpec.enabled vs QuantConfig.enabled mismatch causing a silent dtype_vo no-op — a genuinely novel, sharp bug X misses) and is transparent about what it couldn't verify locally. X counters with a valuable unique catch of its own (new SAGE tests are cuda-marked and never run in the CI lanes that exist) and a more exhaustive systematic sweep, but its sheer claim volume (CI yml internals, role-scoping speculation) is harder to independently confirm and reads as slightly lower-precision per-claim despite being well-cited. Actionability is comparably strong on both sides with concrete diffs and file:line pointers.
